h: Monkey Business and a Potteries Day Out
p: The trick here is to slow right down. The macaques are endlessly entertaining, but you'll see far more if you stand quietly for a few minutes rather than marching round the trail. Watch for mothers carrying their babies, youngsters wrestling and the older monkeys keeping an eye on everyone. Spring and early summer are particularly special, as that's when you're most likely to see tiny babies clinging to their mums.

A few important tips. Keep food and drink tucked away on the trail, because the monkeys are clever and curious and will happily help themselves. Don't try to get too close or touch them, and keep an eye on small children so they stick to the path. It all helps keep the monkeys wild and the visit safe and fun for everyone.
The trail is mostly on woodland paths, so it can be muddy after rain, and you'll want sturdy shoes and a waterproof. Pushchairs can manage, but a rugged one will make life easier.

Once you've done the monkeys, you're in the heart of the Potteries, so make the most of it. World of Wedgwood at Barlaston is just a few miles away, where you can learn about the famous pottery, see craftspeople at work and even have a go at throwing a pot yourself. Gladstone Pottery Museum in Longton is a brilliant, atmospheric museum based in a preserved Victorian pottery factory, complete with bottle kilns. And back at Trentham, the Italian Garden and lakeside walks are perfect for a gentle wander to round off the day.
